summary: L-4 cab on a 41-foot timber tower, Red Butte, Umpqua NF, Douglas County; tower dates to 1953; standing but abandoned; NHLR-registered 2001.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 41-foot treated timber tower (outrigger L-4)
facts.status_note: Standing, but firelookout.com calls it abandoned and the Register says it was used only in emergencies in recent years
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

access.note: Register says the station was used only in emergencies in recent years. No source read says the public can climb it. Cheryl Hill's directory marks the site as legally accessible (Accessible to Public: Yes), which the directory says does not mean access to the lookout itself.

visit.trail_note: Umpqua National Forest, about 24 miles east of Roseburg. No public route or climbing permission found in the sources read.

corrections.why: 6.1 m (20 ft) is the height of the earlier pole tower. The present tower is 41 ft, about 12.5 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 5,223 ft (1,592 m), which matches the record. firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill's directory give 5,275 ft. The record keeps the Register figure.

NHLR and firelookout.com give 1953 for the present tower. A 1943 newspaper item quoted by the Forest Lookouts page says a new tower had been built that year. The sources read do not explain the gap. The record keeps 1953.
NHLR and Cheryl Hill's directory list the tower as standing. firelookout.com calls it abandoned. The record keeps standing, with the abandoned description in status_note.

notes_for_editor: Height correction is the main finding: the record's 6.1 m matches the earlier 20 ft pole tower, not the present 41 ft tower. The 1943 new-tower item conflicts with the 1953 build date and is unexplained in sources read. Rental and access status are unconfirmed. A Forest Service Umpqua camping and cabins page (fs.usda.gov/r06/umpqua/recreation/camping-cabins) appeared in search but was not read. A Library of Congress record for the tower (loc.gov/item/or0645/) returned HTTP 403, so it is not used. Its search snippet describes an L-4 Standard '36 cab on a 41 ft TT-1 tower; check it before relying on that model. Cheryl Hill's Lookout Mountain blog (June 2024) may bear on the planned move but was not read. Photos: NHLR credits a 2015 photo to Dennis Poulin and firelookout.com credits one to Dominic Luebbers; no image URLs were captured, so none are added.
